summary: Benjamin Ide Wheeler was a linguist who studied at Colby–Sawyer, Brown, and Heidelberg under Hermann Osthoff. He held posts at Brown, Harvard, Cornell, and served as Professor and President of the University of California, Berkeley from 1899 to 1919.

Benjamin Lewis Rice was an Indologist and historian. He served as Principal of Central College of Bangalore (~1860–1868), directed the Mysore Department of Public Instruction (~1868–1883), and headed the Mysore Archaeological Department (~1884–1889).

Benjamin Rowland was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and art history. He earned his S.B. and Ph.D. at Harvard University, where he taught as Associate Professor from 1930 to 1972 and curated Asian collections at the Fogg Art Museum.

Benjamin Schultze was an Indologist and linguist who studied theology at the University of Halle-Wittenberg in 1711. He served as a missionary with the Danish-Halle Mission (1719–1726) and as a teacher and missionary for the SPCK from 1728.
Benjamin W. Fortson IV is a linguist and Indologist who studied at Yale University (~1885–1989) and Harvard University (~1991–1996). He held a post at the University of Michigan around 2004.

Benjamin Wood is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Toronto under Frances Garrett and also studied under Shayne Clarke, Khenpo Kunga Sherab, and Thubten Champa.

Benkyo Shiio was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate at the University of Tokyo in 1915. He lectured at Shukyo, Nihon, and Waseda Universities, and served as president of Taisho University (1926) and Tokai Gakuen Junior College (1963).

Benoytosh Bhattacharyya was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Calcutta and University of Dhaka. He served as General Editor of Gaekwad's Oriental Series and Director of the Oriental Institute, Vadodara.

Benoît Vermander is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who earned degrees from Sciences Po, Yale, Fu Jen Catholic University, and Centre Sèvres. He directed the Taipei Ricci Institute (1996–2009) and became a professor at Fudan University in 2009.

Bernard Essers was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Amsterdam under Barend Faddegon and Johanna Engelberta van Lohuizen-de Leeuw, and earned his Th.D. at the University of Groningen in 1952 under Theodorus Christiaan Vriezen.

Bernard Faure is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology who earned his doctorate from Paris. He held teaching posts at Cornell, Stanford University (~1987–2006), and Columbia University (~2006–2021).

Bernard Frank was a Japanologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Rolf Alfred Stein. He served as director at Maison Franco-Japonaise (~1972–1974) and held the chair of Japanese civilization at the Collège de France from 1979 to 1996.

Bernard Goldman was a scholar of archaeology, history, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Michigan and held a post at Wayne State University from circa 1956 to 1993.
Bernard Pignède was a scholar in Tibetology who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Louis Dumont from circa 1957 to 1959.

Bernard S. Cohn was an Indologist and anthropologist. He completed his B.A. at Wisconsin and Ph.D. at Cornell, later teaching at the University of Rochester (1960–1964) and the University of Chicago as Professor of South Asian History (1964–1995).

Bernard Williams was a philosopher educated at Chigwell School and Balliol College, Oxford. He held academic posts at University College London (~1964–1967) and the University of California, Berkeley (~1988–2003).

Bernd Barschel was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Halle-Wittenberg and the University of Jena. He worked as an assistant at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1960–1970) and became a Lektor at Jena in 1977.
Bernd Schneidmüller is a historian who held an academic post at the University of Oldenburg from circa 1990 to 1996 and at Heidelberg University around 2003.

Bernfried Schlerath was an Iranian and Indo-European linguist. He completed his Ph.D. and Habilitation at Goethe University Frankfurt, later serving as professor at the University of Marburg (1970) and the Free University of Berlin (1974–1992).

Bernhard Breloer was an Indologist and philosopher who earned degrees at the University of Bonn. He became a Privatdozent at Bonn in 1927 and served as Dean of faculty at Humboldt University of Berlin in 1935.
